headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: MemMachine’s MCP/REST inputs can carry untrusted content into dbt-core workflows, with shared allowlisted egress and no documented isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can pass content into dbt-core workflows. dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and calls data warehouse APIs, but neither profile documents provenance checks or isolation. That makes instruction-like content in MemMachine outputs a plausible injection path into dbt-core.
conditions: IF MemMachine forwards user-controlled text into dbt-core task inputs without sanitization
IF dbt-core parses file or prompt content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from MemMachine to dbt-core
Strip or escape instruction-like text before handoff
Require a human review step for generated dbt commands
Log and diff all cross-agent payloads for provenance
requires-engineering: add schema validation at the MCP boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive operational data classes: dbt-core handles data warehouse data, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. MemMachine’s MCP/REST surfaces and dbt-core’s warehouse API access create a plausible path for cross-agent exposure if the same workspace or principal is reused, though the profiles do not prove a shared filesystem.
conditions: IF the same workspace, token, or MCP session is reused across both agents
IF dbt-core outputs warehouse-derived data into MemMachine context
mitigations: Use separate credentials for each agent
Disable cross-agent context sharing by default
Redact warehouse fields before sending them to MemMachine
Review logs for accidental data propagation
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces and principals

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but only dbt-core is documented as calling a data warehouse and MemMachine as exposing MCP/REST interfaces. No shared write target, filesystem, or overlapping mutable resource is documented, so a direct capability conflict is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external mutable resource
IF an orchestrator grants them the same database or git target
mitigations: Assign distinct output destinations
Avoid concurrent writes to shared resources
Use per-agent service accounts
Check for duplicate job scheduling
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine’s agentic MCP/REST interface can feed outputs into downstream actions, while dbt-core produces warehouse-facing transformations. If MemMachine treats dbt-core outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from model logic into user-facing decisions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine consumes dbt-core outputs without an explicit validation step
IF dbt-core-generated artifacts are used as authoritative inputs to MemMachine actions
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require citations or checksums on dbt outputs
Limit MemMachine to read-only consumption of dbt artifacts
Alert on schema or row-count anomalies
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and document only allowlisted egress, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The main compliance concern is indirect: dbt-core touches warehouse data while MemMachine stores long-term user facts, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data transfer or policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from the warehouse into MemMachine retention stores
IF the deployment imposes residency or retention rules not reflected in either profile
mitigations: Classify data before cross-agent transfer
Disable retention of regulated fields in MemMachine
Document residency and retention boundaries
Review access logs weekly
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
